missed_findings.title: The 501 handler's request_id fallback can mint an id that exists in no audit row
missed_findings.why_it_matters: The envelope's documented contract is that a caller can quote request_id to correlate with the audit row (schemas/ai.py:104). When AINotImplementedError is raised on a path not wrapped by AIAuditMiddleware, the handler falls back to a fresh uuid4 — an id that matches no audit row, silently breaking that correlation. Today every raiser sits under /api/v1/ai so it is unreachable, but OutboundAIClient.call() also raises AINotImplementedError (outbound_ai_client.py:73) and P10-B is expected to wire that client into service code; the first non-AI-prefixed raise produces orphaned ids with no test to catch it.
missed_findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/core/errors.py:318 --         request_id = getattr(request.state, "request_id", None) or str(uuid.uuid4())
missed_findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish the fallback (e.g. omit request_id, or log a warning when state.request_id is absent) or assert in a test that the only raisers of AINotImplementedError are inside the AI middleware's prefix.

missed_findings.title: AI audit prefix match has no path boundary — over-captures /api/v1/ai* neighbours
missed_findings.why_it_matters: AI_PATH_PREFIX = '/api/v1/ai' is matched with plain startswith (:147-149), so any future route whose path merely begins with those 11 characters (e.g. a hypothetical /api/v1/air-quality) gets unauthenticated body buffering, an audit row with a bogus endpoint value, and an X-Request-ID — none of which belong to it. No such route exists today (the audit router at /api/v1/audit does not collide), so this is a latent trap rather than a live defect.
missed_findings.suggested_fix: Match `path == prefix or path.startswith(prefix + '/')` so the guarded set is exactly the AI subtree.
